Hi Samir / Laura,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we have alignment on success criteria and capacity: 

1) Success criteria (what Acme will use to validate the POC):
   - End-to-end latency <= 350ms p95 for single-session chat under 50 concurrent users.
   - Token-cost per query in line with the budget you gave (~$0.0015/qa average).
   - No functional regressions vs. your baseline model for our core prompts (we agreed to the test set of ~120 prompts).
   - Stable KV cache behavior across session restarts.

2) Evaluation plan & timelines: 
   - Week 0 (this week): baseline data + share MAP and architecture diagram (attached).
   - Week 1-2: POC deploy, reserved GPU pool provisioned, smoke test.
   - Week 3: Load tests and quality evaluation on agreed prompt set; monitor latencies/costs.
   - Week 4: Review readout and decision.

3) Ownership / points of contact:
   - Acme: Samir (technical), Laura (product).
   - Redwood: Marissa (sales/POC lead), Michael Grant (infrastructure lead).

4) Capacity ask (initial):
   - You mentioned 50 concurrent users in peak scenarios. For a conservative starting point we recommend reserving 2 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) with autoscaling to add 1 additional unit for short bursts. We can provide a more detailed sizing once Michael confirms model profile and estimated tokens/sec.

5) Next steps (action items):
   - (Acme) Share the sample prompt set and baseline latency/cost numbers (Samir).
   - (Redwood) Spin up initial reserved pool and share a proposed autoscaling policy (Marissa + Michael).
   - Agree on monitoring dashboard access and evaluation rubric.

Attached: Acme-POC-MAP.pdf, redwood-poc-architecture-diagram.png

If that looks right I can loop in Michael to finalize the GPU sizing and autoscaling behavior later today.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that recap matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the latency KPI should be p95 <= 300ms if possible. Our UX team is strict on that target. If 350ms is more realistic initially, call that "baseline" and we'll treat 300ms as stretch goal.
- Load profile: the 50 concurrent users number is for interactive web sessions; peak bursts could hit ~120 concurrent (short spikes ~2-3 minutes) during demo windows.
- Tokens: average ~450 tokens per user request (including system + user + model output).

Two immediate asks: 
1) Can Redwood support short-lived bursts to ~120 concurrent without manual intervention? We'd prefer autoscaling/burst capacity behavior instead of manual requests.
2) Recommendations on reserved GPUs vs. temporary burst instances and cost tradeoffs — we'd like a short paragraph on the economics and a recommended default for the trial.

I attached the prompt set and a small sample baseline report.

Marissa / team / Samir — quick capacity one-pager below for Acme. High-level recommendations based on 70B-ish model and 450 tokens/request: 

- Conservative reserved baseline: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs. This supports ~40-60 steady concurrent interactive sessions with p95 in the 250-350ms window (depends on sequence lengths).
- Burst plan: enable autoscaling to add up to 2 additional on-demand GPU nodes for short bursts (max concurrent ~120). Autoscaler config: scale-out when queued requests > 15 for 30s, scale-in after 3m idle. Spin-up time for warm nodes ~60-90s in our Dedicated environment; we can pre-warm via a short reserved burst if you need <20s spin-up.
- Autoscaling behavior: continuous batching + KV cache on primary nodes; newly added nodes join with kv-cache-miss initially — expect a brief cold penalty on routing (~100-300ms extra per-token for first few sessions).
- Cost delta (US estimate): 2 reserved GPUs + burst pool ~= $X/hr baseline. Smaller reserved (1 GPU) + on-demand bursts increases burst-hour costs by ~30-50% during sustained bursts; recommended default for trial: 2 reserved + burst cap of 2 on-demand nodes.

Action items we completed: provisioned placeholder offer in our sandbox account; sent one-pager + architecture diagram (attached) to Marissa.

Marissa — we can send this to Samir (with a short paragraph on the cold-warm behavior) and offer an option to pre-warm one node prior to demo windows for predictable latency.

—Michael
